title: U.S. inflation report highlights strain of rising food, energy and housing costs
summary: October consumer prices rose about 0.4% in a month, driven by food, energy and housing, and full-year inflation is now expected to run near 4%, faster than wage growth. Geoff Bennett asks Chicago Fed president Austan Goolsbee what stands out, and Goolsbee calls the report disappointing to the point of worrying, noting that energy and tariff effects have not faded and services prices are still climbing. Goolsbee adds that the AI data center boom is acting like extra stimulus on construction and chip costs, warns that past predictions of short-lived inflation were wrong, and declines to rule anything in or out for the Fed's December rate decision.
focus: Shadow Goolsbee's short answer on the Fed having only one real tool and what cooling demand would mean, and his later reply explaining why calling inflation temporary has backfired before: both are clear, measured central-banker English.

vocab.meaning: Lasting only a short time; temporary.
vocab.context: Goolsbee recalls that earlier forecasts calling price rises short-lived turned out to be wrong.
vocab.example: The board was told the cost spike was transitory, but it has now lasted three quarters.

vocab.meaning: To grow or move faster than something else.
vocab.context: Bennett notes that expected yearly inflation is rising faster than pay.
vocab.example: Competitor revenue has outpaced ours in every region except APAC.

vocab.zh: 令人不安的；令人苦恼的
vocab.context: Goolsbee describes the monthly price figures as a worrying result.
vocab.example: The churn numbers from the pilot market are distressing and need a root-cause review.

vocab.meaning: Very close to being a particular (usually bad) thing.
vocab.context: Goolsbee says the report went beyond disappointing to nearly alarming.
vocab.example: The project's ROI is borderline, so a small cost overrun could kill it.

vocab.meaning: (Of an economy) to grow so fast that prices rise sharply.
vocab.context: The interview weighs whether strong spending is pushing the economy to run too hot.
vocab.example: If the regional economy overheats, wage inflation will erode our labour-cost advantage.

vocab.meaning: Continuing for a long time and hard to get rid of.
vocab.context: Rising service costs are presented as a lasting problem rather than a one-off.
vocab.example: Persistent delays at the port are now a structural issue, not a seasonal one.

vocab.meaning: Money or measures used to encourage economic activity.
vocab.context: Goolsbee compares the AI construction boom's effect to a classic spending boost.
vocab.example: The government stimulus will lift demand for building materials through next year.

vocab.context: He contrasts data center spending with the usual kind of government stimulus.
vocab.example: A conventional cost-cutting programme won't close a gap this large.

vocab.meaning: The US Federal Reserve's two goals: stable prices and maximum employment.
vocab.zh: 双重使命（物价稳定与充分就业）
vocab.context: The discussion turns on which of the Fed's two goals is under more pressure right now.
vocab.example: Like the Fed's dual mandate, our brief balances growth targets against margin protection.

vocab.meaning: Caused by or relating to how much people and firms want to buy.
vocab.context: Goolsbee separates inflation caused by strong buying from inflation caused by rising input costs.
vocab.example: The slowdown looks demand-side, so price cuts alone won't fix volume.

vocab.meaning: A situation where buyers want more than can be supplied, pushing prices up.
vocab.context: The rush to build data centers is described as adding more demand than suppliers can meet.
vocab.example: Excess demand for GPUs gives the supplier strong pricing power this year.

vocab.meaning: Rising prices for services such as health care, rent and repairs.
vocab.context: Goolsbee flags that prices for services are not coming down as hoped.
vocab.example: Services inflation is driving up our outsourced IT and facilities costs.

phrases.meaning: Stay limited to one area without spreading to others.
phrases.zh: 局限在某一领域；不越界
phrases.context: Goolsbee wonders whether price pressure from AI construction will remain confined to that sector.
phrases.example: As long as the price war stays in its lane, our premium segment should be safe.

phrases.phrase: the hair on the back of your neck stands up
phrases.meaning: You feel a strong sense of alarm or warning.
phrases.zh: 令人汗毛直竖；感到警觉
phrases.context: Goolsbee uses this image to say the inflation data should make policymakers uneasy.
phrases.example: When three key accounts asked for contract reviews in one week, the hair on the back of my neck stood up.

phrases.meaning: Limit someone's freedom to act or decide.
phrases.context: He refuses to pre-commit to a rate decision so the Fed keeps its options open.
phrases.example: Don't tie our hands by promising the client a fixed fee before scoping.

phrases.meaning: Being considered as a possible option.
phrases.context: Goolsbee says every policy option remains under consideration for December.
phrases.example: A divestiture of the logistics unit is now on the table.

phrases.meaning: Something many people are thinking or worrying about.
phrases.zh: 大家都在关注的；众人心头的事
phrases.context: He says rising costs are a top worry for businesses and families in the Midwest.
phrases.example: Tariffs were on everyone's mind at the leadership offsite.
